questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Coming to a big city in Europe were I could experience new cultures and also its near position to other capitals in mid and eastern Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any particular assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The webpage of the university linked to some different opportunities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular, there is not much difference from living in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You needed to sign up for a lot of different courses. If enough spots were available you would get the courses but if more students were interested in the course than there were spots it was a lottery.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Course describtion.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for more ECTS than you need so you are sure to get enough. You can see how many students that have signed up for the different courses and compare to spots available. Remember to check if the time courses take place overlap as quite a lot of the courses do that.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You needed to have around 10 courses, as each course was 2-4 ECTS and that reflected the academic level of the courses as they were general to small to give more than an overview on the specific subject.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professors were generally very enthusiastic and knew a lot about their courses as it was themselves who designed them, contrary to UCPH.  However, I missed having some books/reading material about the subjects as it often just was presentations by the teachers.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Discussion, Negotiation and Presentation in English
2. Private Law Theory
3. Introduction to English Contract and Tort Law
4. M & A International Part II - Competition Law (cartel-agreements, mergers)
5. Mediation for Lawyers
6. Comparative and Uniform Secured Finance Law
7. European and International Business and Technology Law Seminar
8. Public Markets, Securities Regulation and Corporate Governance
9. Drafting and Negotiating Cross-border M & A and Joint Venture Contracts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found the "Public Markets, Securities Regulation and Corporate Governance" and "Mediation for Lawyers" to be very interestering with great professors. I especially think that the Mediation course will be beneficial for all law student regardless of legal field of interest. I also found the Drafting and Negotiation M&A Contracts course very interestering.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping were more expensive than what I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university had a sports club that offered almost every sport to a very good price.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports club and just experience the city in general

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the city, especially the museums etc. and the wine fields just outside the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, not that big of a difference from Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them in class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were generally open and talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be in good time with applying for scholarships, housing etc.
2. Apply for more ECTS than you need.
3. Enjoy.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the city and meeting new friends from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The practical stuff in the beginning/before the semester.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
